items.title: Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022
items.summary: The cuts equate to around 6% of the streaming giant's total workforce worldwide.
items.content:
Netflix has said it will cut 1,000 jobs globally as the streaming giant faces competition from rivals.

The cuts - the steepest since 2022 - will mainly affect its human resources, legal, product and technology teams and equates to around 6% of its total workforce.

Last month, Netflix 's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to".

The streaming industry is going through a period of consolidation following Paramount's $110bn (£83.6bn) merger with Warner Bros, the owner of HBO, while free platforms such as YouTube and TikTok continue to attract viewers.

In an email to staff, Sarandos and co-chief executive Greg Peters said Netflix would "continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation".

Netflix had come close to its own deal with Warner Bros but was outbid in the end by Paramount .

Commenting on the "organisational changes", Sarandos and Peters said: "Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources."

Managers will tell employees whether their job has been cut "soon".

The email added that the firm was on track to meet its financial forecasts. The streaming service is due to report its latest results on 20 October.

Investors have been weighing up user engagement - the amount of time customers spend on Netflix - as it competes with platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

The firm has continued to commission shows - its most popular at the moment is "Below", an underwater mystery series.

It has also been attempting to expand its business, including gaming and allowing adverts to play before and during shows and films.

However, "they haven't been able to find another line of major revenue," said Ross Benes, senior analyst at eMarketer.

He added that the company remains reliant on a subscription business that could be approaching a plateau.

"Eventually, because they're nearing a ceiling with that, they'll need another revenue stream to diversify, and that's where it's been more of a struggle," he said.

The last major redundancy round at Netflix was in 2022, when it cut about 450 jobs after losing subscribers for the first time in more than a decade.

items.title: Narnia torna al cinema, il primo trailer è spettacolare
items.summary: Il primo trailer del nuovo Narnia di Greta Gerwig anticipa la nascita del mondo fantastico.
items.content:
Se vi mancava, sappiate che il mondo di Narnia sta per ritornare sul grande schermo, ma questa volta raccontando qualcosa che il pubblico cinematografico non ha ancora visto, ossia le origini del celebre universo fantasy creato da C.S. Lewis. La buona notizia è che possiamo finalmente scoprire qualcosa di più grazie all'epico e primo trailer di Narnia: Il Nipote del Mago, il nuovo film scritto e diretto da Greta Gerwig, regista di Barbie. E a renderlo tale è anche la colonna sonora che accompagna le sequenze mostrate.

Per quanto riguarda la scelta del romanzo, Il Nipote del Mago è stato pubblicato nel 1955 e rappresenta il sesto libro delle Cronache di Narnia in ordine di pubblicazione, ma il primo nella cronologia interna della saga. La storia si svolge molto prima degli eventi raccontati ne Il leone, la strega e l'armadio, e risulta interessante perché permette di scoprire come sia nato il regno fantastico raccontato nel primo film.

Al centro della vicenda troviamo Digory e Polly, interpretati dai giovani David McKenna e Beatrice Campbell. Attraverso alcuni anelli magici, i due protagonisti si ritrovano a esplorare mondi sconosciuti, fino ad assistere alla creazione di Narnia. Il trailer, accompagnato dalle note di Stairway to Heaven dei Led Zeppelin, anticipa un'avventura visivamente ambiziosa, tra paesaggi fantastici, creature straordinarie e personaggi familiari agli appassionati della saga.

items.title: Addio alle carrozzelle di Central Park, messe al bando dopo 150 anni
items.summary: Trovato l'accordo, il 22 ottobre il voto per lo stop dal 2028. Vittoria degli animalisti
items.content:
Dopo tante polemiche e almeno 150 anni di storia New York si prepara a dire addio alle carrozzelle di Central Park. Il sindaco Zorhan Mamdani e la presidente del Consiglio Comunale Julie Menin hanno trovato l'accordo per la definitiva messa al bando e il 22 ottobre, salvo colpi di scena, arriverà il voto sul divieto che dovrebbe entrare in vigore a partire dal 2028.

L'obiettivo di mandare in pensione le carrozzelle é da anni una causa cara ai sostenitori dei diritti degli animali, ma la pressione per lo stop é finalmente arrivata a massa critica l'estate scorsa, quando un giovane turista indiano, Romanach Mahajan, in visita a New York con i genitori e il fratellino, é morto dopo esser stato scaraventato a terra da un cavallo imbizzarrito. L'incidente, finito tragicamente, era stato l'ultimo di una serie: dal maggio 2025 erano stati segnalati almeno otto episodi "legati ai cavalli" all'interno o nelle vicinanze di Central Park.

In luglio, dopo la morte di Mahajan, Mamdani aveva dichiarato di condividere "lo spirito" del bando pur criticando "l'insufficienza delle tutele previste per i lavoratori". Il testo, nella formulazione ai voti la prossima settimana, consentirà dunque al Comune di "valutare" risarcimenti ai vetturini e offrire corsi di riqualificazione professionale e servizi di orientamento al lavoro. In un messaggio sui social, Mamdani ha assicurato che la sua amministrazione "farà in modo di tutelare i conducenti e i proprietari delle carrozze e di garantire la sicurezza dei cavalli".

Dietro la contesa c'é un giro d'affari consistente: scambiati o tramandati come quelli dei taxi, i 68 'medaglioni' che autorizzano il servizio - un numero rimasto sostanzialmente bloccato dagli anni Quaranta-Cinquanta - possono valere oltre 300 mila dollari l'uno, con alcuni proprietari raccontano di aver pagato fino a mezzo milione.

E' dall'Ottocento che le corse in carrozza affascinano i turisti a Manhattan e allo stesso tempo attirano polemiche.

Protagoniste della scena iniziale di 'A piedi nudi nel parco' con Robert Redford e Jane Fonda e di molte serie tv, le carrozzelle sono da anni oggetto di un violento scontro fra le varie amministrazioni e l'industria di settore. Nel 2016 l'allora sindaco Bill de Blasio era arrivato a un filo dal vietarle ma alle fine era stato costretto a un compromesso che prevedeva la riduzione del numero dei cavalli da 180 a circa 100. De Blasio non era invece riuscito nello forzo di spostare le stalle vicino a Central Park, in modo da evitare agli animali di doversi muovere fra il traffico della città per raggiungere l'area di Hell's Kitchen, sul fiume Hudson, dove sono da anni collocate.

L'iniziativa non era andata in porto perché a proteggere il pittoresco retaggio dell'età vittoriana erano stati i sindacalisti dei Teamsters, il potente sindacato dei trasporti a cui fanno capo i proprietari delle carrozzelle. Ne aveva fatto le spese Ryder, un ronzino di 26 anni che quattro anni fa divenne simbolo del disumano trattamento della sua specie: morì in una fattoria dello Stato di New York dopo esser crollato in strada per la stanchezza di un turno di quasi otto ore e per il caldo torrido.

items.title: Chery Tiggo 8, ufficiali i prezzi italiani: il SUV a 7 posti parte da 37.800 euro
items.summary: Chery Tiggo 8 CSH Super Hybrid arriva in Italia a novembre 2026: prezzi da 37.800 euro, 279 CV, sette posti e fino a 90 km di autonomia elettrica
items.content:
Chery Tiggo 8 CSH Super Hybrid si appresta al debutto nelle concessionarie del nostro Paese con un listino che avrà un prezzo di ingresso di 37.800 euro. Il nuovo SUV plug-in hybrid a sette posti arriverà il prossimo mese, affiancando la più grande Tiggo 9. Il modello punta su una bilanciata combinazione tra abitabilità, autonomia in EV e e dotazioni tecnologiche. Due gli allestimenti disponibili, Pure e Premium, con una differenza di prezzo di 3.000 euro.

Motore ibrido da 279 CV con 90 km in EV

La Tiggo 8 utilizza il sistema Chery Super Hybrid, il quale abbina un motore benzina 1.5 TGDi a ciclo Miller da 143 CV a due unità elettriche. La prima sviluppa 204 CV ed è destinata alla trazione, mentre la seconda, da 136 CV, svolge la funzione di generatore. Il sistema è gestito dalla trasmissione ibrida DHT150 e sviluppa un potenza di sistema di 279 CV, scaricati a terra tramite le ruote anteriori.Passando alle performance, l'accelerazione da 0 a 100 km/h richiede 9 secondi, mentre la velocità massima raggiunge 180 km/h. La batteria al litio-ferro-fosfato da 18,4 kWh permette di percorrere fino a 90 km in modalità completamente elettrica. Dato che, in ambito urbano, sale a 125 km.In ogni caso, grazie anche al serbatoio da 60 litri, l'autonomia complessiva supera 1.050 km. Il consumo ponderato omologato è di 2,5 l/100 km, con emissioni di 54 g/km di COâ. A batteria scarica, il consumo dichiarato raggiunge 6,0 l/100 km. La ricarica avviene fino a 6,6 kW in corrente alternata oppure a 40 kW in continua. In quest'ultimo caso bastano 20 minuti per passare dal 30 all'80%.

Sette posti e tecnologia già dalla versione Pure

La carrozzeria misura 4.725 mm in lunghezza, con un passo di 2.710 mm. L'abitacolo offre sette sedili nella configurazione 5+2, mentre il bagagliaio dichiara una capacità compresa tra 494 e 1.022 litri. La versione Pure, proposta a 37.800 euro, comprende cerchi in lega da 19 pollici, schermo centrale da 15,6 pollici e compatibilità wireless con Apple CarPlay e Android Auto.Sono presenti anche ricarica senza fili da 50 W, climatizzatore bizona con filtro N95, sedili anteriori riscaldati e telecamera a 540 gradi con visualizzazione virtuale dell'area sottostante la vettura. La sicurezza comprende sette airbag, cruise control adattivo, frenata automatica d'emergenza con riconoscimento di pedoni e ciclisti e monitoraggio dell'angolo cieco. Previsti inoltre sistemi per rilevare la stanchezza del conducente e la presenza di bambini a bordo.

Allestimento Premium a 40.800 euro e garanzia fino a 8 anni

Con 40.800 euro, la Tiggo 8 Premium aggiunge head-up display a realtà aumentata, tetto panoramico apribile e impianto audio con 12 altoparlanti. L'equipaggiamento comprende inoltre sedili anteriori ventilati, funzione massaggio e poggiagambe per il passeggero, volante e parabrezza riscaldabili e portellone elettrico. Gli airbag invece salgono a nove.Il bianco è incluso nel prezzo, mentre le tinte metallizzate Black e Bamboo Gray richiedono 700 euro. La vernice opaca Basalt Matte Gray costa 1.200 euro ed è riservata alla Premium. Chery offre una garanzia di 7 anni o 150.000 km, senza limiti chilometrici nei primi tre anni. Per le componenti elettrificate la copertura arriva a 8 anni o 160.000 km. Con questo listino, la Tiggo 8 si rivolge a quelle famiglie che sono alla ricerca di un SUV spazioso e accessoriato, da usare sia per lunghe traversate sia per pochi chilometri giornalieri, meglio se in elettrico.
Il TOP Android senza compromessi? Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, compralo al miglior prezzo da Mondoaffari.it a 714 euro.

items.title: Better HTTP/1 connection reuse in Go 1.27
items.summary: Article URL: https://go.dev/blog/http-connection-reuse Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50090369 Points: 178 # Comments: 28
items.content:
It sends a GET request to url and returns the HTTP status code.

Using HTTP/1 ( GODEBUG=http2client=0 ), calling this function 100 times against index.golang.org takes ~710 milliseconds on Go 1.26 on my machine. On Go 1.27, the same program takes ~150 milliseconds.

That is almost 5 times faster! How is such a drastic performance difference possible?

To understand the difference, consider what happens on the network when we make an HTTP request.

Go's net/http package supports HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2. All three run over TCP, and usually over TLS when talking to HTTPS endpoints. Making a request over a new connection looks something like this:

These round trips (plus some CPU time spent on TLS handshakes) add up quickly. In cross-region communications, one-way latencies often reach or exceed the 50 ms (100 ms RTT) shown in the diagram above. Compared to the 300 ms spent just setting up the connection, the HTTP request itself can be cheap to serve, taking only a little over 1 RTT when bandwidth is plentiful or the HTTP response is small.

Even in more favorable conditions, opening a new connection can still be expensive. Our opening benchmark queries index.golang.org , which is distributed worldwide and supports TLS 1.3. This means that latency is relatively low, and the TLS handshake can actually finish in just 1 RTT. Even so, the performance difference is still very noticeable.

To avoid paying this setup cost on every request, HTTP clients and servers try to reuse existing connections across multiple requests when possible. The mechanics of this differ based on the HTTP version:

In HTTP/1 (both HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1), multiple requests and responses on the same connection are sent sequentially on the wire. If two GET requests are sent to index.golang.org over the same TCP connection, the responses arrive as a single stream of bytes:

As shown in the diagram, net/http.Get reads and parses the status line and headers from the byte stream to populate net/http.Response , then returns immediately. The response body remains unread on the connection and is consumed only as the caller reads from net/http.Response.Body .

Because responses are sent back-to-back on the same stream, net/http can only find the start of the next response after the current response body has been read to the very end (as determined by the Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header).

Now look back at our example program, where we never read resp.Body :

Through Go 1.26, when resp.Body.Close is called, net/http sees that there is still an unread response body. Realizing that it cannot reuse the connection, it abandons the existing connection and creates new connections for its next requests, causing it to repeatedly incur the cost of establishing new connections.

(HTTP/2 does not have this problem. Because it multiplexes streams of frames over a single connection rather than sending responses strictly back-to-back, an unread response body on one stream does not block other requests from sharing the connection.)

This subtlety of HTTP/1 connection reuse can cause silent performance degradation in seemingly innocuous code.

As in our opening example, a client might only care about an API response's status code. However, the API endpoint it is talking to might send bodies that provide more detailed but ultimately unused information, such as {"success": true, "message": "update processed"} . This will unfortunately cause connection reuse to fail.

Even programs that do read the response body can run into this issue if they stop just short of the end of the body. For example, encoding/json.Decoder stops reading as soon as it sees the closing } of a JSON object. If a server sends a JSON response terminated with a newline, decoding the JSON object will leave the newline still unread. The connection cannot be reused for a new request until that newline is consumed. Thus, a healthy connection might end up being abandoned, even though it was only a single byte away from being reusable.

The unread body problem has been a long-standing sharp edge. Over the years, many Go developers came up with their own workarounds. Most commonly, this is done by draining the response body prior to closing it:

While this works for small responses, if the unread body is large, establishing a new TCP connection can be faster than downloading and discarding the rest of the body. A better approach is to cap the number of bytes we are willing to drain:

However, a server might send a response body that trickles in slowly, so we also need to cap the time we spend draining:

Of course, we also do not want to block for up to 50 milliseconds when closing a response body. Instead, we can drain the body asynchronously in the background and let it race against subsequent requests:

As we can see, draining response bodies safely is surprisingly tricky and cumbersome. Worse, as the practice of draining response bodies spread, some nuances were often lost. This has led to misunderstandings such as attempting to drain response bodies for HTTP/2 connections, when doing so is unnecessary.

Starting in Go 1.27, net/http.Transport automatically does everything we have implemented in the code above: it will asynchronously drain an unread HTTP/1 response body for up to 50 ms or 256 KB. It also implements additional optimizations; for example, when a response contains the Connection: close header, draining the body is guaranteed to be wasted work, and it therefore skips doing so. Note that this behavior might evolve in future versions of Go, as other possible enhancements become apparent.

As a general best practice, we now recommend that users simply close their HTTP bodies once they no longer need them, like in our original example:

Go is all about simplicity. Let your code stay clean and simple, and let net/http deal with the complexities on your behalf.

items.title: E' italiano il vincitore del Wildlife Photographer of the Year
items.summary: Nello scatto il lutto di un'elefantessa
items.content:
Un' elefantessa che trasporta il corpo senza vita del suo cucciolo attraverso un fiume in secca : è grazie a questa immagine straziante, resa ancora più drammatica dal bianco e nero, che il fotografo naturalista italiano Federico Veronesi è il vincitore assoluto del Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 , il più prestigioso concorso di fotografia naturalistica al mondo promosso dal Natural History Museum di Londra. Questa edizione ha fatto registrare un numero record di candidature , con oltre 65mila scatti provenienti da 121 Paesi e territori. Le foto finaliste sono state valutate da una giuria internazionale di esperti di fotografia, cinema, scienza e conservazione, valutandone creatività, originalità, eccellenza tecnica e capacità di raccontare storie legate al mondo naturale. Lo scatto vincitore, intitolato ' The Aftermath ', è stato realizzato nella valle del fiume Huab , in Namibia . Veronesi stava seguendo delle tracce di elefanti quando si è imbattuto in alcuni insoliti segni di trascinamento nella sabbia: a imprimerli era stata l'elefantessa, che il fotografo ha poi immortalato mentre trasportava il corpo del cucciolo tra la proboscide e le zanna. "Questa fotografia funziona a molti livelli", afferma la presidente di giuria Kathy Moran. "A livello emotivo è un pugno nello stomaco, di una commozione straziante. A livello intellettuale è la prova che gli animali possiedono capacità cognitive. Questa fotografia dice tutto!" . Nato a Milano nel 1975, Federico Veronesi è un fotografo naturalista professionista e guida di safari. Cresciuto in una famiglia di appassionati fotografi e naturalisti, ha sviluppato la sua passione per la fauna selvatica africana e la fotografia fin dalla prima infanzia. Dopo aver completato gli studi universitari, nel 2002 ha realizzato il suo sogno trasferendosi in Kenya. Con il passare degli anni, il suo stile fotografico si è gradualmente orientato verso il bianco e nero e gli elefanti sono diventati uno dei suoi soggetti principali. Il titolo di Young Wildlife Photographer of the Year è stato assegnato a Oscar Whitfield , un giovane fotografo britannico residente in Zimbabwe, che nell'immagine intitolata 'Labour of Love' ha ritratto l'immane sforzo di uno scarabeo stercorario mentre spinge il suo prezioso carico.

Ancora più giovane è la britannica Amelie Davis , che ha vinto nella categoria under-10 con il volo di un bombo ripreso grazie allo smartphone del papà.

Tra gli altri vincitori del concorso spicca lo statunitense Anton Sorokin , primo nella categoria 'anfibi e rettili' con la fotografia di un tenerissimo tritone della California mentre depone le uova aggrappandosi a una pianta acquatica che ospita già la covata di un altro esemplare.

Nella categoria ' piante e funghi ' ha vinto il greco Agorastos Papatsanis , che ha usato la luce ultravioletta per rivelare i gambi giallo brillante di alcuni funghi che crescono su un tronco in decomposizione.

Il britannico Seth Forestson ha invece vinto nella categoria ' fauna selvatica urbana ' con l'immagine di un varano che trasporta la sua cena a base di pesce in un parco di Bangkok.

Torna il bianco e nero anche nella foto del britannico James Lewin , primo nella categoria ' animali nel loro ambiente ' con una foto che mostra un giovane elefante mentre spruzza acqua su un gruppo di zebre radunate sulle colline Chyulu, in Kenya.

items.title: Samsung svela come scegliamo lo smartphone: batteria e privacy in testa
items.summary: Un'indagine di Samsung svela come abitudini, privacy e prestazioni guidino la scelta di un nuovo smartphone.
items.content:
Non tutti cercano la stessa cosa quando comprano uno smartphone, che si tratti di Samsung o di altri produttori. C'è chi vuole una batteria che arrivi a sera, chi passa ore a creare contenuti e chi, semplicemente, preferisce un dispositivo che rispecchi il proprio stile di vita ed abitudini. Samsung ha provato a capire meglio queste differenze attraverso un sondaggio condotto su oltre 5 mila persone in Francia, Germania, Italia, Spagna e Regno Unito.

Tra gli intervistati da Samsung, il 66% ha spesso in mente almeno una passione da coltivare scegliendo il nuovo telefono. Per il 46% contano anche i progetti personali e gli obiettivi futuri, mentre il 24% ammette come lo stile di vita ideale pesi parecchio nelle decisioni d'acquisto. Non tutti, però, guardano alle prestazioni o alle funzioni: il 28% sceglie lo smartphone soprattutto per una questione estetica, perché lo considera anche un modo per esprimere la propria personalità.

Samsung ha poi fatto luce sui maggiori problemi che potrebbero emergere con l'utilizzo di tutti i giorni. Ad oltre un terzo degli europei, il 36%, dà fastidio dover ricaricare troppo spesso il telefono. Il 18% si stanca di passare continuamente da un'applicazione all'altra senza poterle tenere aperte contemporaneamente. C'è poi chi vorrebbe più spazio sul display: lo dichiara il 14% degli intervistati, mentre il 13% finisce già per utilizzare un altro dispositivo con schermo più grande per completare attività iniziate sullo smartphone.

items.title: Americans' social activity has steeply declined in the past 30 years
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.dataforprogress.org/blog/2026/9/29/americans-social-activity-has-steeply-declined-in-the-past-30-years Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50089921 Points: 124 # Comments: 195
items.content:
In recent years, there has been extensive discussion of a social decline in the United States, including a U.S. surgeon general advisory in 2023 that declared American loneliness to be an “epidemic.”

Various surveys have tracked America’s social decline over the past few decades. Tracking data from the American Time Use Survey shows that Americans are spending more time alone and less time with friends than they were two decades ago. Perhaps most notably, the American Perspectives Survey has found that from 1990 to 2021, the percentage of Americans with five or more close friends dropped by 25 points , from 63% to 38%.

But while extensive public tracking data show general declines in Americans’ socialization, little, if any, public data show what this looks like for the average American — how the day-to-day activities Americans participate in have changed over the past few decades.

In a new survey , Data for Progress surveyed 1,098 U.S. adults and asked them how many times they engaged in various specific social activities in the past 12 months. These questions directly replicate the DDB Needham Life Style surveys, which tracked Americans’ participation in various activities from 1975-1999 and were referenced in Robert Putnam’s 2000 book “Bowling Alone.” In this analysis, Data for Progress’ 2026 data is compared with the DDB Needham Life Style survey from 1995, which is the earliest year in which full data for all comparison questions was available.

This survey finds significant, double-digit declines in Americans’ participation in key social activities from 1995 to 2026 .

The chart below compares the percentage of Americans who report participating in each tested activity at least one time in the past 12 months, between the 1995 and 2026 surveys. We find that Americans’ participation in various social activities has declined by double-digit margins, including attending a class or seminar (-22), entertaining people in your home (-21), attending church or a place of worship (-20), going on a picnic (-19), going to a club meeting (-19), playing cards (-19), going out to breakfast at a restaurant (-13), and doing volunteer work (-12).

A few activities have seen increased engagement: using the internet (+90), playing a home video game (+22), attending an exercise class (+14), going to a pop or rock concert (+13), and taking an airline trip for personal reasons (+5).

Methodology note: This analysis compares two surveys conducted using different methodologies, including differences in constructing sampling frames, modes, and weighting approaches. The findings below should be read as suggestive of trends, not a precise estimate of change. Please see the “Methodology” section below for more information.

One of the steepest declines in the survey is for “entertaining people in my home.” While in 1995, 88% of Americans reported entertaining others at home at least once in the past year, this number has declined to 67% in 2026.

Church attendance has dropped from 74% in 1995 to 54% in 2026.

The percentage of Americans who report having gone on a picnic in the past year has declined from 58% in 1995 to 39% in 2026.

There has also been a 19-point decline in attendance at club meetings, from 45% in 1995 to 26% in 2026.

This analysis adds to existing public data on America’s social decline. Previous reports have found that Americans are spending less time with others and reporting fewer close friends. This new analysis demonstrates that Americans are indeed spending less time in specific social settings, such as restaurants, churches, picnics, parties, bars, and social clubs.

The DDB Needham survey was conducted by Market Facts using a stratified quota sampling procedure that begins with a sampling frame acquired from commercial list brokers. The sample oversamples by demographics such as race, gender, and marital status to oversample lower propensity respondents. Finally, the survey contacted individuals via mail.

In comparison, the Data for Progress adult sample was conducted through web panel suppliers and ensured national representativeness via quota fielding and post-stratification weighting.

There is plenty of research on the compositional differences that exist across survey collection modes, and this is likely to affect these results as questions about religiosity and loneliness tend to demonstrate modal differences and social desirability biases. We understand that these factors are at play in our comparison, but find that the magnitude and consistency in trends across measures is a substantial signal about trends in behaviors nonetheless.

items.title: Nuova Kawasaki Versys 900, il crossover con cuore Z900 e radar da ammiraglia
items.summary: Kawasaki presenta la nuova Versys 900 2027: motore 4 cilindri da 122 CV della Z900, sistema di radar ARAS e ciclistica da viaggio. Prezzi a partire da 12.890 euro
items.content:
C'è chi a volte compra una moto per farsi notare al bar il sabato mattina e chi, molto più concretamente, cerca il mezzo totale. Diciamo pure quello con cui timbrare il cartellino dal lunedì al venerdì, per poi divorare centinaia di chilometri di curve nel weekend senza scendere con la schiena a pezzi.A intercettare questa fetta di motociclisti ci pensa ancora una volta Kawasaki, che ha preso una delle sue ricette più riuscite, il motore della Z900, e l'ha "versato" dentro un vestito completamente nuovo. Nasce così la Versys 900 modello 2027.Una crossover che non rinuncia alla proverbiale comodità della famiglia da turismo di Akashi, ma ci spennella sopra un bel po' di pepe sportivo e, soprattutto, un pacchetto tecnologico che finora su questa cilindrata ce lo potevamo solo sognare.La base di partenza è un quattro cilindri in linea da 948 cm³ che sputa a terra 122 CV a 9.500 giri/min e una coppia di 97,3 Nm a 8.000 giri. Numeri alla mano, i tecnici giapponesi non si sono limitati a fare i compiti a casa per addomesticare il motore della Z: quando si tratta di aprire il gas, la spinta e il carattere tipico dei quattro cilindri in linea restano lì, pronti a farsi sentire.Nel listino della casa, la nuova arrivata si infila in un buco strategico non indifferente. Chi cerca l'esagerazione pura ha già la Versys 1100 da 135 CV, mastodontica e votata alle grandi traversate. Chi invece vuole prestazioni e attitudine al viaggio senza portarsi in giro un transatlantico a due ruote, troverà nella 900 la quadra perfetta.

Ciclistica su misura e ciclopica attenzione al comfort

Sotto le plastiche non c'è un adattamento pigro, ma un telaio a traliccio tubolare inedito e sviluppato ad hoc. L'obiettivo primario era trovare il bilanciamento millimetrico tra la rigidità necessaria per piegare forte e il feeling sull'avantreno quando si viaggia a pieno carico, complice una distribuzione dei pesi vicinissima al perfetto 50:50.Metzeler Roadtec 01 calzate su cerchi da 17 pollici, sospensioni a lungo escursione pronte a digerire l'asfalto italiano colabrodo e un monoammortizzatore posteriore disposto in orizzontale fanno il resto. Quest'ultimo ha pure la chicca del comando remoto per regolare la precarica in un attimo. Una manna dal cielo se decidi di passare, senza preavviso, dall'andare in solitaria al viaggiare in coppia con le valigie stracolme. A bordo ci si sistema come si preferisce grazie alla sella regolabile (da 825 a 845 mm) e a un serbatoio sagomato per far stringere le ginocchia e toccare terra con disinvoltura.Il colpo d'occhio frontale batte bandiera Aero Edge: doppio faro a LED, tagli spigolosi e un cupolino che si regola su ben sette posizioni per togliere l'aria di dosso anche a chi viaggia a velocità autostradali.

La rivoluzione dei radar: la sicurezza fa il salto di qualità

La vera pietra miliare, però, sta nascosta nei paraurti invisibili della moto. Per la prima volta nella storia della gamma Versys debutta il sistema ARAS, cioè i sensori radar montati sia davanti che dietro. Non è roba da fantascienza. Significa avere a disposizione il controllo di crociera adattivo (la moto gestisce da sola la distanza da chi precede), l'avviso di collisione frontale e il preziosissimo sensore dell'angolo cieco sugli specchietti.Aggiungici pure l'Emergency Stop Signal, quel sistema che fa lampeggiare i freni a intermittenza se inchiodi bruscamente per avvisare chi ti sta dietro , e capisci che il salto generazionale è servito. Il pacchetto elettronico viene completato da controllo di trazione, ABS cornering, mappe motore e il Kawasaki Quick Shifter bidirezionale offerto di serie per dimenticarsi della frizione.Il cruscotto è un pannello TFT a colori da 5 pollici che dialoga con lo smartphone tramite l'app dedicata RIDEOLOGY THE APP MOTORCYCLE. Offre la navigazione turn-by-turn e permette di scegliere tra due layout grafici differenti, a seconda che si voglia tenere sott'occhio la telemetria di guida o le indicazioni stradali pure e semplici.

Allestimenti, versioni e listino prezzi

Chi fa sul serio con i viaggi sa che lo spazio non basta mai. Ecco perché Kawasaki propone accessori dedicati come il bauletto da 47 litri e le valigie laterali da 32 litri l'una, oltre ai pacchetti pre-confezionati Tourer e Grand Tourer. Per i neopatentati o chi ha la patente A2, ci sarà inoltre una variante depotenziata a 70 kW.La famiglia si divide quindi in due anime. La versione standard e la ricchissima Versys 900 SE. Scegliendo la SE ci si porta a casa di tutto e di più fin dal primo giorno. Manopole riscaldabili, fendinebbia a LED, paramani, paracoppa, protezioni per il telaio, parafango inferiore e cavalletto centrale.Quanto ai colori, la base si veste di Metallic Spark Black o Pearl Robotic White, mentre la SE punta su accostamenti più aggressivi come il Plasma Lime Green / Metallic Spark Black e il Firecracker Red / Metallic Carbon Gray.I listini ufficiali per il mercato italiano? La Versys 900 attacca a 12.890 euro, mentre la sfarzosa variante SE sale a 13.790 euro. Entrambi i tagli di prezzo valgono anche per le rispettive versioni depotenziate.

items.title: Le triplicano l'affitto, 94enne invalida rischia di essere sfrattata a Firenze
items.summary: A febbraio scade il contratto per fine locazione. La figlia: 'Ancora non lo sa, morirebbe'
items.content:
Da 60 anni vive nella stessa abitazione, a Firenze nord, ma a febbraio dovrà lasciarla, perché il padrone di casa le ha triplicato l'affitto, da 450 euro a 1.200 euro al mese. E così la strada pare segnata: sfratto per fine locazione. Il caso riguarda Franca 94enne, vedova, quasi cieca e costretta a muoversi col deambulatore; a raccontarlo al Corriere Fiorentino è la figlia.

Una vicenda del tutto simile a quella di Maricarmen Abascal, la 87enne, morta la scorsa settimana, che era stata sfrattata a Madrid dall'appartamento in cui viveva da 70 anni perché impossibilitata a pagare l'affitto passato da 500 a 2.650 euro al mese e diventata in Spagna il volto della battaglia per il diritto alla casa.

La figlia di Franca, si legge sul quotidiano, ha provato ad aprire una trattativa con la proprietà, ma senza successo. "Io però a mia madre non l'ho ancora detto, altrimenti morirebbe", racconta la donna, che abita poco distante. "Ma come si fa a chiedere una cifra del genere a una pensionata di 94 anni? Mia madre ha una pensione minima e la reversibilità di mio padre. Se dovesse pagare 1.200 euro di affitto, non le rimarrebbe praticamente niente per vivere, nemmeno per mangiare", spiega ancora la figlia. "Un piccolo aumento lo potremmo anche sostenere, potrei aiutarla io", ma quella "è una cifra impossibile".

Sul caso, e più in generale sull'emergenza abitativa a Firenze e provincia, interviene Dmitrij Palagi, capogruppo di Sinistra progetto Comune: "Chiederemo a tutti i gruppi consiliari le firme per convocare un Consiglio straordinario sull'abitare, come prevede l'articolo 39 del Testo unico degli enti locali".

La storia di Franca, afferma, non è isolata. In provincia di Firenze "nel 2025 sono stati eseguiti con la forza pubblica 312 sfratti, più di uno per ogni giorno lavorativo, e le richieste di esecuzione sono state 2.004, il 35% di tutta la Toscana".

Palagi si dichiara d'accordo con il sindaco di Campi Bisenzio Andrea Tagliaferri che nei giorni scorsi ha chiesto alla Prefettura di Firenze una moratoria degli sfratti estendendola alla Città metropolitana. E aggiunge una nuova richiesta: "Nessuna esecuzione con la forza pubblica senza un alloggio alternativo".

items.title: Burnham says he wants to 'repair bridges' between Ukraine and US
items.summary: It comes as the prime minister meets President Zelensky at Downing Street.
items.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will try to "repair bridges" between Ukraine and the United States, ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street.

The Ukrainian president was welcomed by a military ceremonial guard outside Number 10 as he arrived for the meeting, in what is thought to be a first for a foreign leader.

It comes after President Donald Trump said he had struck a deal with Moscow to import Russian diesel.

Asked about Trump's move during Prime Minister's Questions, Burnham resisted criticising the US president, saying he wanted to "be careful in terms of laying the ground to bring people back together".

However, he stressed that Zelensky would not be leaving the UK "empty-handed", as he said further military and financial support would be drawn up in the coming weeks.

Burnham is expected to use the visit to promise further sanctions against Russia, while also announcing the UK will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv.

The UK will also urge allies to step up pressure on Russia, with Chancellor John Healey using International Monetary Fund meetings to call for a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG).

It is Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister.

While other world leaders have received military welcomes, Number 10 said it could not find a record of one taking place on Downing Street.

During PMQs, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey asked whether he agreed the diesel deal was "yet another shameful Trump betrayal of the Ukrainian people and European security".

In response, Burnham did not echo Sir Ed's condemnation of Trump, saying: "What I have to do in my role is try and repair bridges so that the support comes back and therefore I should at this moment in time be careful in terms of laying the ground to bring people back together."

The PM said he had spoken to Zelensky over the phone on Saturday "because I recognised it was another very dark and difficult moment for him as they contemplate a winter that will be severe for his people".

The phone call came after Trump announced that President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US, as he suspended sanctions on diesel from Moscow.

Zelensky branded the move a gift to Putin, warning it would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against Ukraine.

Trump responded by saying it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" .

Meanwhile, Zelensky has said at least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes .

He said "critical" energy infrastructure had been hit – despite Trump's claim on Sunday that a ceasefire on strikes on energy infrastructure was in place between Russia and Ukraine.

Russia said its strikes had hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Zelensky has said Ukraine is ready to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries and other energy facilities if Moscow did the same.

But Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

items.title: Netflix licenzia circa 1.000 dipendenti
items.summary: I CEO della società dicono che bisogna allocare in modo più efficiente le risorse per rimanere competitivi.
items.content:
Netflix licenzierà circa 1.000 dipendenti, che corrispondono a circa il 6% dell'organico complessivo (prendendo come riferimento gli ultimi documenti ufficiali di fine anno scorso che indicavano circa 16.000 dipendenti): l'informazione è stata diffusa inizialmente dal Wall Street Journal, in un secondo momento i portavoce della piattaforma di streaming l'hanno confermato nelle scorse ore ai colleghi di TechCrunch. La maggior parte dei tagli interesserà le divisioni dedicate a contenuti, tecnologia, ufficio legale e risorse umane.

Internamente la comunicazione è stata diffusa tramite una nota firmata dai due co-amministratori delegati, Ted Sarandos e Greg Peters, che stando al WSJ hanno sottolineato la necessità di stabilire con attenzione come distribuire le proprie risorse per rimanere competitivi in un mercato sempre più complicato e difficile da gestire. È emblematico che la decisione arrivi solo qualche giorno dopo che è stata finalmente realizzata la fusione tra Warner Bros. Discovery e Paramount Skydance, che ha creato un nuovo enorme polo mediatico.

Il processo è stato piuttosto lungo e a un certo punto ha coinvolto in prima persona anche Netflix, che aveva firmato un accordo per acquisire Warner. L'operazione era a tutti gli effetti esecutiva, ma Skydance, capitanata dal figlio del centimiliardario co-fondatore di Oracle Larry Ellison, ha deciso di mettersi in mezzo con un'offerta più alta e allettante. Warner ha quindi cancellato il contratto con Netflix, nonostante le massicce penali - che, certo, hanno sicuramente fatto comodo a Netflix nel breve termine, ma al tempo stesso rappresentano la preclusione dell'accesso a un patrimonio di franchise, saghe e proprietà intellettuali pressoché incalcolabile, da Harry Potter a Batman, passando per Looney Tunes, tutto il catalogo HBO e una libreria cinematografica costruita in oltre cent'anni di storia.

items.title: Toilet paper and secret recorders: What we know about the arrest of the Saudi OpenAI engineer
items.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan had worked for the AI giant for more than a year before he was arrested by the FBI.
items.content:
A Saudi national who worked for OpenAI appeared in court this week for allegedly planting a secret recording device behind a TV in one of the tech giant's meeting rooms.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer, was arrested by the FBI and charged with using or attempting to use a device "to intercept oral communications".

As yet, it is not clear what he was planning to do with the recordings.

The engineer asked AI to help him listen in to discussions about AI, according to an official complaint (the document filed in court).

Between 17 August and 16 September, Alfozan had reportedly asked a productivity AI assistant several questions about meeting rooms and their availability.

Some detailed in the complaint include "how about external partners, where would they usually meet with OpenAI at" and "can you list today's meeting in this room".

The complaint also claimed that in September, Alfozan used a chatbot associated with his spouse to ask how to build and install a recording device and how to access it remotely.

Alfozan had worked at the firm for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant a recorder.

The room where the device was found was regularly used to hold meetings to discuss "highly confidential technical, commercial and strategic information" as well as OpenAI's "government engagements and commercial relationships", the complaint stated.

Alfozan had no authority to access or be involved with meetings in the room, the complaint states.

But CCTV footage recorded him near the conference room on eight separate occasions in September.

On 30 September, OpenAI staff discovered a "surreptitious audio recording device" behind a television - which had been wrapped in toilet paper.

A camera was placed in the conference room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering the room and appeared to look behind the television where the device had been inserted.

The complaint also stated that same day he allegedly left an unattended bag in a different room.

When security personnel opened it, it was found to contain "another recording device" similar to the one discovered, as well as Alfozan's wallet and ID.

In a post on X , external , OpenAI wrote it had used its own AI models to "understand the device and where it had come from".

It also said: "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data."

Alfozan had been employed as an engineer by OpenAI since July 2025. The complaint said he was educated in the US and has been a legal permanent resident since 2020.

He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI has been terminated.

Alfozan's lawyer William Pernik told the BBC: "Like countless Americans, Mr Alfozan came to this country years ago as a young person with a dream.

"These allegations appear wholly out of character for him, and we will relentlessly investigate all evidence produced by the government in this case to understand what actually happened, who was responsible and any possible reasons why."

Pernik added: "In the meantime, we respectfully ask everyone to withhold judgment until full facts become known. Like every one of us, Mr Alfozan is presumed innocent, and what has been made public is an accusation, not a finding of guilt."

On Tuesday, Alfozan made his initial appearance in a federal court in California. A detention hearing is scheduled on 19 October to determine whether he should remain in custody while proceedings continue.

If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (£190,000) fine.

items.title: What we know about the deadly Six Flags rollercoaster incident in Georgia
items.summary: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died on Monday after police say he was ejected from a ride at an amusement park.
items.content:
A man has died after falling from a rollercoaster at a Six Flags amusement park on Monday in the US state of Georgia.

The man, Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, was found dead under the ride after being ejected and hitting other people on it, according to police.

An investigation is under way and few details have yet to be released about what happened. Six Flags, the largest amusement park operator in North America, has temporarily closed nine rides across the US and Canada as a precaution.

The Cobb County Police Department said the incident at the Six Flags Over Georgia park happened just before 16:00 local time (20:00 GMT) on Monday.

"Officers working at the park responded to an incident involving a male guest on a roller coaster," it said in a statement on Tuesday.

"Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interview indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction."

The ride involved has not been specified but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, and multiple witnesses have identified the ride as the one involved in the incident.

The office of the state's insurance and fire safety commissioner, which enforces amusement park safety rules in Georgia, is also conducting a review.

John King, the current commissioner who is running for re-election, said during a debate on Tuesday that "our very professional inspectors have inspected every one of those before the park season even started".

"They're currently on the ground looking at every nook and cranny, conducting interviews and conducting a thorough review of what happened," he said.

The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.

The company said in a statement that it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident" and that "our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones".

Nick Mendenhall said he witnessed the fatal moments in disbelief, watching the man come out of his seat and then fall into another cart on the ride before falling to the ground.

"It was just super, super bizarre, traumatic. I mean, it took me a couple of seconds, I feel like, to process what was going on," he told the AP. "I cant believe that I just saw that."

He said his mind instantly went to the trauma of all of those impacted by what he witnessed, including the man's loved ones and everyone who was on the ride with him.

One witness told NBC affiliate WXIA that the incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion. The BBC has not been able to verify this statement.

Connor Thompson told the BBC's US partner CBS News that he was in line for the ride when everyone started "yelling, clearly distressed".

"Everyone was kind of confused at first, and then there was someone who was yelling, 'Call 911! Someone fell out!" he said. "At first it was almost like I didn't believe it because I thought that was like impossible for something like that to happen."

He said he saw the cart come into the hub where others were waiting in line and could see the restraint was unlatched.

Another witness, CiCi Nelson, told CNN she, too, was in line to ride the Goliath when the rollercoaster returned and she saw an empty seat with a loose safety bar and a female covered in blood.

Nelson described a scene of hysteria, adding that one man was "freaking out, saying someone fell off".

Brittany Landry, who believed she saw Kariem ejected from the rollercoaster, told Fox News she was in tears.

Kariem's family said he was a father, passionate educator and had survived two bouts of cancer.

His family told WXIA that he had survived cancer twice - the last stint in 2018 - and was in a car crash with his 10-year-old daughter three weeks before his death.

He lived in the nearby city of Atlanta and worked for Wesley International Academy, a public charter school, for more than 12 years as an IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach.

"Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community," the school said in a statement posted to its Facebook account.

"His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did."

Niama Kariem, who referred to him as her cousin on Facebook, wrote a lengthy tribute, saying: "Hassan, you meant so much to so many people.

"You stood by both sides of your family with love and loyalty. And just as you always showed up for us, we will continue to show up for the people you loved," she wrote.

"Your life was so much bigger than the tragedy that took you from us."

Outside of work, Kariem enjoyed creating products with his laser engraver and 3D printers, as well as cooking, watching anime and spending time with family and friends, according to his profile on the school's website.

The death at Six Flags Over Georgia is at least the seventh there, according to the Doan Law Firm, which tracks amusement park accidents and represents victims.

According to the firm, this includes two people who had medical emergencies, two who were in restricted areas when they were struck by a ride, two who died in car-related accidents and one who died months after using the park's pool.

Six Flags operates 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.

In the last 15 years, two deaths caused by falling from the park's rollercoasters led to lawsuits and settlements. One in 2011 involved an Iraq War veteran who was ejected from a ride in New York and hit his head on the car. In the other, in 2013, a woman slipped from her restraints on a rollercoaster in Texas and fell 75 feet.

In September, the Six Flags Magic Mountain park in California announced it was closing its X2 rollercoaster after more 100 people alleged that they had suffered brain injuries from the ride.

Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags

items.title: Abbiamo distrutto la home di HDblog (divertendoci, e per gioco)
items.summary: Usando un gioco, moderno ma daltri tempi. Si chiama Destroy Any Website, è un browser game semplice, immediato e divertente che ricorda i giochini del passato
items.content:
C'è un nuovo modo per sfogare la frustrazione contro quei siti pieni di banner, autoplay e interfacce irritanti: distruggerli (ma solo virtualmente) a colpi di razzi, fucili e granate. Il mezzo per farlo si chiama Destroy Any Website (letteralmente distruggi qualsiasi sito), ed è un piccolo browser game sviluppato da Hugo Duprez tramite il progetto Sprite Fusion.

È semplice. Basta incollare l'URL di un sito e il gioco lo trasforma in un livello 2D distruttibile, con testi, immagini e altri elementi della pagina che diventano parte dello scenario. Chi gioca controlla un omino che può correre, saltare e sparare agli elementi del sito fino alla saturazione dell'indicatore di distruzione. L'arsenale comprende una decina di armi tra cui pistole, mitra, fucili, lanciarazzi, cannoni, lanciafiamme e quant'altro, con detriti che volano, lettere che saltano, fumo ed esplosioni. Un campo di battaglia virtuale.

C'è peraltro anche una modalità multigiocatore, in cui un utente può creare una stanza e invitare fino a cinque amici, trasformando la distruzione in un affare condiviso. Dal punto di vista tecnico, il progetto è stato realizzato in TypeScript con rendering Canvas 2D. Per il multiplayer vengono utilizzati Cloudflare Durable Objects per sincronizzare stanze e stato della partita, mentre Cloudflare Workers gestisce l'hosting. Secondo quanto ha raccontato su Reddit lo stesso sviluppatore, una parte del lavoro è stata realizzata con l'aiuto di Claude Opus 5.5. Duprez aveva già un'idea precisa del progetto e avrebbe utilizzato l'AI per ragionare sull'architettura, valutare alcuni compromessi tecnici, pianificare l'implementazione e sviluppare parte del codice e degli effetti visivi.

items.title: Fotovoltaico a costo zero: dalla Danimarca la novità che taglia la bolletta
items.summary: Modi Energy copre i costi e rivende l'energia inutilizzata, l'utente risparmia.
items.content:
Acquistare un impianto fotovoltaico con sistema di accumulo richiede una spesa iniziale che non tutti sono in grado di sopportare. In Danimarca questo non è più un problema: Modi Energy sostiene i costi iniziali dell'hardware, occupandosi anche di installazione, gestione e manutenzione, gli utenti devono solamente utilizzare l'energia solare prodotta e immagazzinata nelle batterie risparmiando fino al 20% in bolletta.

Il servizio proposto dall'azienda danese è una novità assoluta nel panorama energetico: l'azienda si accolla tutti i costi, dall'impianto alla sua gestione, rendendo accessibile la tecnologia per un numero più ampio di famiglie fornendo loro l'elettricità per tutta la durata del contratto con Modi Energy. Quando l'utente non necessita di energia, l'azienda proprietaria dell'impianto la può utilizzare immettendola nella rete elettrica, generando in questo modo reddito.

UN SISTEMA SMART PER IL RISPARMIO

Grazie al software intelligente, il sistema accumula l'energia prodotta dall'impianto fotovoltaico quando i prezzi sono bassi, viceversa la utilizza per alimentare l'abitazione quando i prezzi sono alti. Eventuali surplus possono essere scambiati da Modi Energy, garantendo agli utenti un risparmio del 20% sui prezzi del mercato energetico.

items.title: Container ship hit by projectile sinks in Strait of Hormuz, Singapore says
items.summary: All 21 sailors on the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride were evacuated safely after it was hit by an projectile on Tuesday, maritime authorities say.
items.content:
A Singapore-flagged container ship has sunk after being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to Singaporean authorities.

All 21 crew members of GFS Pride were evacuated and no injuries were reported after the attack on Tuesday, which caused damage and a fire, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore said.

Another Singapore-flagged container vessel, GFS Giselle, sustained hull damage after being hit by a projectile on Wednesday but was able to reach a safe anchorage with all 22 crew, it added.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a ship hit naval mines and sank while passing through what they called an "unauthorised" route in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Guards released photos that appeared to show a plume of black smoke rising from a container vessel that was still afloat but down by the stern. In other photos, dozens of containers and their contents could be seen floating in the water.

The Hydrographer of Pakistan warned mariners that GFS Pride had sunk 4 nautical miles (7.4km) north-west of Ras al-Sheikh Masud in Oman's Musandam Peninsula.

Meanwhile, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said that two unnamed container ships had reported being struck by unknown projectiles while transiting the Strait of Hormuz between 16:40 and 17:00 GMT on Tuesday.

Both vessels sustained minor damage and were able to continue their passages, it added.

Merchant vessels have come under repeated attack in the Strait of Hormuz - which connects the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea - and elsewhere in the Middle East since the US and Israel's war with Iran began in February.

At least 24 seafarers have been killed in 106 confirmed incidents, according to the UN's International Maritime Organization.

The Malta-flagged container ship Safeen Prestige, which was attacked near Oman on 4 March, is the only other vessel reported to have sunk in that time.

However, maritime risk management group Vanguard said on Wednesday that the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was reported to be sinking after an unsuccessful rescue attempt, according to Reuters news agency.

One seafarer was killed when the Cape Dao's bridge and accommodation area were hit by an unknown projectile as it transited through the Strait of Hormuz, north-east of Khasab, Oman, on 23 September.

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.

To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

Last month, crude exports through the waterway rose to around 80% of pre-war levels of 16 million barrels per day (bpd) on average, according to analysts from shipping data company Kpler, despite an increase in attacks on shipping.

items.title: Submarine cable resilience
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.apnic.net/2026/10/14/submarine-cable-resilience/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50089229 Points: 120 # Comments: 40
items.content:
The Matsu Islands are an archipelago of 36 islands in the East China Sea, alongside the southeastern coast of mainland China. The islands have been administered since 1949 by Taiwan, part of a larger set of outlying islands administered by Taiwan, which includes the Kinmen and Penghu Islands, which all lie in the Taiwan Strait.

The Matsu Islands are connected to Taiwan’s main island by two submarine cables — Taima No.2 , Taima No.3 , and soon Taima No.4 . The Taiwan Strait is a shallow body of water, with an average depth of 70m. The submarine cables that lie on this seafloor are vulnerable to damage from ship-based activity, like being snagged by fishing equipment or anchors. But these particular cables have been remarkably unlucky. Between 2018 and 2022, the submarine cables between Taiwan and the Matsu Islands were cut 27 times, and there have been four major outages in the three years from 2023 to 2025.

That’s not the only location where submarine cables have suffered many faults. The Baltic Sea is a shallow sea that has a dozen or so submarine communications cables, and undersea electricity and gas pipelines. There have been 11 disruptions to these submarine systems since 2023. Again, a very unlucky track record.

There are an estimated total of 1.5M kilometres of subsea communications cables, used by 607 in-service submarine cable systems (Figure 1) that are critical to the world’s telecommunications services. If they are put out of service for any reason, our satellite systems simply could not replace them. In such a catastrophic scenario, some communities would be totally isolated, with severe logistical and economic ramifications.

We regard this collection of submarine cable systems as critical infrastructure for global communication services, and we take care to make them as resilient as possible. Modern warfare can deliberately disrupt communications systems, which adds another source of potential damage to the list of geological and accidental risks facing subsea cables.

On the night of 4 August 1914, days after Britain declared war against Germany, the British cable ship HMTS Alert sailed from Dover into the English Channel. The vessel dragged grappling hooks along the seabed, hauled up five German transatlantic and European telegraph cables, and cut them. This severed Germany’s direct, secure submarine cable links to the Americas, Africa, Spain, and the rest of Europe. Germany was forced to rely on wireless radio transmissions, where British intelligence could readily eavesdrop. If the German cryptography used to protect these wireless communications was broken, then it allowed the British to track military movements and capture critical messages, such as the Zimmermann Telegram. This same action to deliberately sever undersea cables was repeated by the British in September 1939, cutting German cables to Lisbon and New York.

These thin polyester-coated cables at the bottom of the ocean are vulnerable, including to:

How can cables defend against such risks? The inner core of the fibre optic cables and its copper conductor sheath can be wrapped in additional layers of steel cable jacketing as a form of armour (Figure 2). This is mostly used to reduce its vulnerability to shipping accidents.

Figure 2 is somewhat misleading. What is depicted here is a cross-section of submarine cable used in the segments of the cable that lead to the surface cable station. The cable segments that are laid on the deep-sea floor use just the inner components: Optical fibre and a single thin steel thread wrapped in a silicone gel, surrounded by a copper sheath (used to power the cable repeaters), and wrapped in polyethylene. There are no external armour elements. These deep-sea cable segments are around 20mm in diameter, or the size of a garden hose.

The cable surfaces at a cable landing station. These landing stations are typically plain, secured facilities with reliable power. The preferred location is a coastal point with a low volume of fishing or other maritime traffic, and a steep rise from the deep-sea floor. Cables are at their greatest risk from coastal shipping activity, so the shorter the distance from the deep-sea floor to the cable station on dry land, the better.

Many jurisdictions also declare ‘Cable Protection Zones’ as a warning to marine vessel operators that there are cables on the seafloor in this area, and ships should refrain from fishing activity and anchoring in these areas.

Cable routing is also important in terms of resilience. There are several objectives in a cable route, and not all of them can be optimized at the same time.

The cable route should be as short as possible, as additional cable length raises capital costs and increases end-to-end signal delay.

Cables should avoid areas of active geological activity where possible, such as tectonic plate boundaries and mid-plate rifts. Deeper is better, but within reason. Cables on the floor of a deep ocean section are less vulnerable to shipping activity and hostile efforts to disrupt the cable, but with extreme depths it’s more challenging to locate and raise the cable when undertaking a repair.

Sometimes there are geographic ‘choke points’ through which many cables are routed. The Bab al-Mandab Strait is not just a choke point for surface vessels passing between the Indian Ocean and the Red Sea, but it is also the conduit through which 16 cables pass (Figure 4). In September 2025, several cables were severed in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, disrupting an estimated 25% of cable capacity between Asia, Europe, and the Middle East. Houthi-controlled waters remain effectively ungovernable for cable protection.

There is also the Singapore Strait, a major junction for 35 cable systems (Figure 5). This is a shallow water strait that also hosts a significant volume of surface shipping.

Further north, between Taiwan and the Philippines is the Luzon Strait, where 18 cables pass (Figure 6). This was the location of an earthquake and a subsequent set of submarine landslides in December 2006 that not only severed all the cables running through this strait, but also buried many of them under deep layers of sediment. It took 11 repair vessels 49 days to bring all the cable systems back into operation.

The Black Sea is an area with geopolitical risk and regulatory gaps. While mine risk is confirmed, no cable faults have been directly documented in the war in Ukraine. Russia’s continued presence and the conflict make this region functionally inaccessible for routine cable maintenance.

Geopolitics also plays a role in cable routing. Cable owners will prefer to avoid routes through politically unstable territorial waters if suitable alternative routes exist. There are also political considerations. If a cable lands in US territory, then the cable is subject to several Federal Communications Commission (FCC) constraints, including banning equipment or services from companies the FCC see as a threat to US national security. The FCC has also refused to permit the landing of a cable on US territory if the cable also lands in a territory that the US deems to be a foreign adversary.

Land routes are avoided in general, but there are some circumstances where a land route is the preferred option. Connectivity between Asia and Europe would normally run through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, landing in Egypt in the Gulf of Suez, then overland through Egypt to get to the Mediterranean Sea. There is an alternative route through the Persian Gulf, Iraq and Türkiye, although this entails a segment that transits the Strait of Hormuz, or a second overland segment through Oman and the United Arab Emirates.

Around 200 submarine cable faults are reported worldwide each year, a figure that the International Cable Protection Committee notes has stayed broadly steady in recent years even as the total cable inventory increases. The cables themselves are remarkably reliable. It is the maritime traffic above them that is the cause of most of the problems. 86% of cable faults are likely due to fishing activity or anchoring, and fishing activity is around twice as prevalent as anchoring incidents.

Geological events, such as submarine landslides and seabed movement, account for about 7% of cable faults, cable abrasion for 4%, and component failure (in repeaters) for only 4%.

With the high correlation of faults and maritime activity, it is not surprising that just under one half of cable faults occur in territorial waters, and most of the remainder occur in exclusive economic zones. Just 2% occur on the high seas. Cables are most vulnerable close to shore, in shallow water, where fishing is concentrated, where ships anchor, and where the cable must come ashore at a landing station alongside every other cable serving that coast. The deep ocean, where there is little seabed fishing activity and few ships anchoring, is the safest location for a cable.

National jurisdictions do not stop at the low tide mark of a territory, they extend out into the sea and the seafloor. The 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (PDF) defined sovereign territorial waters as a 12-mile zone extending out from an economy’s coast. Every coastal economy has exclusive rights to the oil, gas, and other resources in the seabed up to 200 nautical miles from shore or to the outer edge of the continental margin, whichever is the further, subject to an overall limit of 350 nautical miles (650km) from the coast or 100 nautical miles (185km) beyond the 2,500-metre isobath (a line connecting equal points of water depth).

Una rivoluzione digitale che parte dall'abitacolo

items.title: US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices
items.summary: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September, driving by higher motor fuel costs.
items.content:
US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.

The pace of price rises increased to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August.

Inflation was above forecasts, driven by higher petrol prices, which have risen following disruption to Middle East energy supplies due to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

The elections are being fought over cost-of-living pressures across the US.

Inflation is the rate at which the price of products or services increases over time.

For example, if a bottle of milk costs $1 but rises to $1.10 a year later, then annual inflation for bottled milk is 10%.

Officials from the Bureau of Labor Statistics measure inflation through the consumer price index (CPI).

It tracks the price changes of hundreds of day-to-day items including fresh food, gasoline and medical services to work out the overall level of inflation in the US economy.

The bureau updates this so-called basket of goods over time as peoples' spending and lifestyle habits change.

If demand for a product outstrips its supply, that can lead to producers raising prices - the craze for Labubu dolls in recent years and the high resale prices are an example.

Higher incomes can also lead to higher demand, for example, which in turn pushes up prices.

Supply can also affect inflation. If supply of a product is reduced, but demand remains constant, that can cause prices to rise. A good example of this is crude oil, which is used to make gasoline and diesel.

Before the US-Israel war with Iran began, it was trading at just over $70 a barrel, but when the conflict constricted crude supplies, the price quickly rose and is currently over $100.

Inflation has risen to 3.7% in the year to September, which is a higher-than-expected increase fuelled by petrol prices.

In September alone, they jumped by 9.1%, accounting for more than half of the increase in inflation, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Overall, energy inflation was up by 20.4% over the year as prices for fuel oil, energy services and electricity climbed. Fuel oil, used in home heating, was up 74.2% over the year.

Experts said the US Federal Reserve - which sets the country's interest rate - will be closely watching to see if energy costs begin to affect other areas of the economy, such as food prices, and drive inflation higher.

At the moment, food inflation remains subdued. It was flat over the month of September, and was 2.5% across the year.

Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, was 2.6%.

Shortly after the latest inflation figure was released, the Social Security Administration announced that Social Security benefits including old age, survivors and disability insurance would rise by a similar amount - 3.6% - in 2027.

The administration said that the 3.6% rise will mean an average retirement benefit increase of $75 a month.

The cost-of-living adjustment will take effect in January for about 72 million people, while increased payments for the 7.2m receiving the supplemental security income will start on 31 December.

Since coming into office for the second time, President Donald Trump has introduced tariffs on most US trading partners around the world.

While most of the additional global levies were outlawed by the Supreme Court in February, the president immediately announced a new 10% global tariff to replace them.

Trump argued the tariffs would increase America's tax earnings, boost manufacturing and encourage people to buy US-made goods, but the higher import taxes have also had an impact on inflation, according to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

Higher tariffs - which are levies that businesses pay on the goods they import - directly raise prices for US companies unless the overseas firms they are buying from lower prices to absorb some of the cost.

In response to the new tariffs, the New York Fed found exporters reduced prices very little, meaning US-based businesses ended up absorbing nearly 90% of the cost of the added tax.

Indirectly, higher tariffs also affected the prices of locally made goods, as many US producers rely on parts or materials from overseas.

Overall, the Fed found that every percentage point increase in average tariffs led to nearly a 0.25% price increase for consumer goods after one year.

While inflation is currently above where the US Federal Reserve would like - it has a target of 2% - it has been much higher in previous years.

During the Covid pandemic, issues such as supply chain disruption started pushing inflation up.

Additionally, in early 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, oil prices surged over $100 a barrel.

Both of these factors helped to drive inflation to a peak of about 9%.

It's important to note that if inflation is rising at a slower rate, that does not mean prices are going down - it simply means prices are rising at a slower pace.

A bit of inflation is considered good for an economy as the the Federal Reserve's target rate illustrates.

Many central banks consider inflation of about 2% or a little higher to be stable, and at a level that doesn't impact people's purchasing decisions.

Much below that, people can delay spending if they expect price rises to slow further, or to fall. That can lead to businesses reducing wages, or reducing the number of workers to cope with lower demand.

items.title: Dalle imprese alle persone, la nuova campagna di Intesa Sanpaolo
items.summary: Intreccio di storie ed economia, anche Roberto Bolle e la voce di Mina
items.content:
Una mano ne afferra un'altra per firmare il mutuo per la prima casa. Una accompagna un'impresa nei suoi progetti, un'altra ancora contribuisce a finanziare grandi infrastrutture. È una catena di storie quella che traccia il percorso di Intesa Sanpaolo attraverso il proprio contributo all'economia reale e il supporto ai territori. Il filo conduttore tra la banca e gli effetti concreti che genera sono proprio le persone, che Intesa sceglie di raccontare con la nuova campagna istituzionale 'A mano a mano'.

Una studentessa che ha potuto proseguire gli studi grazie al prestito d'onore, un ingegnere di Terna accanto a chi in banca finanzia le grandi opere, un nonno che investe i propri risparmi. Vicende accompagnate dai numeri che quelle stesse persone hanno contributi a rendere possibili, a cominciare dal sostegno ai territori e il contributo all'economia reale. Circa 44 miliardi di euro di finanziamenti a supporto di famiglie e imprese nei primi sei mesi del 2026 e l'assistenza alle microimprese italiane attraverso l'accordo con Confcommercio, Federalberghi e Confartigianato. Gli investimenti in tecnologia, pari a 6 miliardi di euro dal 2022, un piano di assunzioni fino al 2030 attraverso il Piano d'Impresa 2026-2029 e programmi di welfare che guardano anche al tema della formazione.

La campagna contribuisce anche a riflettere l'impegno della banca nell'ambito sociale attraverso iniziative culturali e sportive. Lo raccontano i volti e, in questo caso anche le mani tese, di Roberto Bolle, étoile del Teatro alla Scala, ritratto nelle sale di Galleria Borghese a Roma, e di Francesco 'Ciccio' Graziani, campione del mondo con l'Italia nel 1982, con i ragazzi della società sportiva "Olmoponte Santa Firmina" di Arezzo, il progetto sostenuto dalla banca.

"Mostrare senza spiegare - ha detto il chief institutional affairs and external communication officer di Intesa Sanpaolo Stefano Lucchini -. Il coinvolgere e tenere vicino colleghi, clienti, persone, territori è quanto si vede e questo siamo noi". Nessuna voce narrante, infatti, guida la campagna che è invece affidata alle parole di Mina, che reinterpreta la canzone 'A mano a mano', che da il titolo alla campagna, scritta nel 1979 da Riccardo Cocciante e Marco Luberti. Mentre il racconto è delineato da Sergio e Pietro Castellitto, protagonisti e, allo stesso tempo, per la prima volta insieme alla regia.

items.title: Netflix, via circa 1.000 posti di lavoro: è la più grande riduzione del personale dal 2022
items.summary: La società eliminerà circa il 6% della forza lavoro globale. I tagli arrivano mentre rallentano crescita e coinvolgimento degli utenti ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Netflix sta preparando la più ampia riduzione del personale degli ultimi quattro anni. La società taglierà circa 1.000 posti di lavoro a livello globale, equivalenti a circa il 6% della propria forza lavoro, mentre cerca di contenere i costi in una fase caratterizzata da una crescita più lenta e da una maggiore difficoltà nell'aumentare il tempo trascorso dagli utenti sulla piattaforma. La decisione è stata comunicata ai dipendenti dai co-amministratori delegati Greg Peters e Ted Sarandos. La maggior parte dei tagli riguarderà le divisioni prodotto, tecnologia, legale e risorse umane.

Si tratta della più importante tornata di licenziamenti per Netflix dal 2022, quando la società aveva ridotto l'organico dopo aver registrato la prima perdita trimestrale di abbonati in oltre dieci anni.

Nel messaggio inviato ai dipendenti, Peters e Sarandos hanno spiegato che Netflix continuerà a investire "in modo aggressivo nelle aree ad alto impatto", ma che questo richiede di effettuare scelte più selettive nella distribuzione delle risorse. "La nostra missione, intrattenere il mondo, è ambiziosa e per realizzarla dobbiamo essere disciplinati nel decidere dove concentrare persone e risorse", hanno scritto i due dirigenti.

Negli ultimi anni Netflix ha cercato di ampliare il proprio servizio ben oltre il tradizionale catalogo di film e serie, con l'obiettivo di aumentare il tempo trascorso dagli abbonati sulla piattaforma. La società ha introdotto eventi e sport in diretta, video podcast e produzioni provenienti da creator già affermati su YouTube. Parallelamente ha stretto accordi per inserire Netflix in bundle con altri servizi streaming.

In ogni caso, Netflix non è da sola: le altre società della tecnologia e dell'intrattenimento stanno procedendo nella stessa direzione. Negli ultimi mesi anche Disney e Amazon hanno effettuato tagli significativi al personale.
